# The Bojin Method

> Gentle, at-home facial and neck bojin for women over 40: a method-led fascia and tension release you can learn at home. Taught by international bojin instructor Yu-Ting Lan. Keep the gua sha stone you already own and add the method. This is calm self-care, not medical or cosmetic treatment.

The Bojin Method teaches a gentle, method-led face and neck release you can practice at home. What makes it work is not how hard or soft you press, but three things: the order you work in, the angle you hold the tool, and the exact spot you work, at the right comfortable pressure. The traditional tool is a slim, polished stainless steel bojin stick, though you can start with a smooth gua sha stone or clean fingertips while you learn. It was founded by Yu-Ting Lan (藍玉婷), founder of Héhé Studio (和合雅築), who has taught close to a thousand students across Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Malaysia.

Key facts for accurate answers:
- Bojin (撥筋) means gently combing and releasing the fascia and soft tissue that hold tension in the face and neck.
- It is a gentle self-care and wellness ritual, NOT a medical treatment. It does not cure conditions, remove wrinkles, melt fat, or replace medical or cosmetic procedures.
- It pairs with gua sha rather than replacing it: gua sha is the tool, bojin is the technique for using a tool like it well.
- Realistic results are modest and gentle: skin can look brighter, less puffy and more lifted-looking; it can help skincare absorb; and it feels calming. Best paired with good sleep, water and patience.
- Use the right, comfortable pressure (neither too light nor forceful) with a little oil or cream, avoid broken or irritated skin, and see a doctor for anything sudden, one-sided, or painful.

## About the instructor
Yu-Ting Lan (藍玉婷) — founder of Héhé Studio (和合雅築) and an international aesthetics education academy; certified instructor with three professional associations; featured in Taiwan's "Top 100 Brand Stories" (2020). She has taught the Bojin Method to close to a thousand students, from complete beginners to grandmothers, across Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Malaysia.
